No support for growth. As a generator installation company, we have used Invoice2go for over a year and have grown significantly during that time. While the platform itself has been helpful, we have encountered a major issue with payment processing limits.

Our business regularly invoices approximately $15,000 per generator installation, yet our monthly payout limit remains capped at $50,000. This means our funds are frequently held back, creating unnecessary cash flow challenges and forcing us to wait extended periods to access money that rightfully belongs to our business.

What has been most disappointing is the lack of resolution despite multiple attempts to address the issue. We have submitted requests to increase our payout limits, provided banking references, and even had our bank verify our financial standing and available funds across multiple accounts. Unfortunately, none of these efforts resulted in any meaningful action or communication.

For a growing business, reliable access to earned funds is critical. The inability to increase reasonable payout limits, combined with the lack of responsiveness, has been extremely frustrating and has negatively impacted our experience with the platform.

I hope Invoice2go will improve its support process and provide more flexibility for established businesses that have demonstrated a strong payment history and financial stability.

My Recent Experience With Invoice2go’s Payment System. After more than a decade using Invoice2go to manage invoicing for my restoration business, I have always appreciated the platform for its practicality and ease of use. However, I recently encountered a situation that raised serious concerns about their new credit-card processing system and the quality of their customer support.

Invoice2go has recently resumed accepting credit-card payments through a third-party processor, Bill.com. Unfortunately, this change created unexpected complications that affected both me and my client. One of my customers did not recognize the charge from Bill.com on her American Express statement, and she disputed the transaction even though the payment was legitimately made for services I provided.

Once I learned of the issue, I immediately clarified with my client that Bill.com was simply Invoice2go’s new processor. She confirmed the payment was valid and even sent a written statement explaining that she had authorized the charge. I forwarded her letter to Invoice2go, expecting a quick resolution.

Instead, the process became increasingly frustrating. Invoice2go refused to release the funds and requested an additional letter directly from my client’s American Express account an unreasonable and inconvenient requirement for both my client and for me. Despite my effort to cooperate, I was eventually forced to obtain a copy of the original transaction directly from my client’s AMEX statement and send it to Invoice2go as further proof.

Even after providing that documentation, Invoice2go informed me that they would still hold the $3,600 payment for 90 days. The communication throughout the entire situation was slow, unclear, and extremely unhelpful. At no point did I feel supported as a long-standing customer who has trusted this platform for more than ten years.

A payment processor’s responsibility is not only to protect against fraud but also to support legitimate businesses when disputes arise. Holding funds for such an extended period after the client confirms the legitimacy of the transaction does not represent best practices. Combined with poor communication and unreasonable documentation demands, this experience has caused me to seriously reconsider whether Invoice2go’s current payment system is suitable for a professional business.

After years of loyalty, this was truly disappointing. I hope Invoice2go reviews these internal procedures and improves both transparency and customer service so that other small businesses do not face the same unnecessary inconvenience.
